name: doc-step
purpose: One numbered step of a `DocSteps` walkthrough: the circled index, the rail that continues to the next step, the step heading, and any content the author nests underneath. The number and the last-step mark come from the `DocSteps` context — the step registers itself during setup and reads its reactive index back, so an author writes a title and never a number. Rendered outside a `DocSteps` provider it throws (`useDocStepsContext must be used within DocSteps.`) instead of rendering unnumbered.
useWhen: Only as a direct child of `DocSteps`, one per instruction the reader performs.
avoidWhen: Anywhere outside a `DocSteps` column — the context composable throws by design.
For a checklist entry or a feature bullet — a step claims an order and a number.
related: DocSteps` — the sibling root that numbers this; it provides the context this step registers with.
DocProse` — the step heading marks itself `data-doc-chrome`, so prose rules stop at its edge.
bestPractices: Lead the title with the verb and keep it to one line of instruction.
Put elaboration — prose, a code block, another component — in the body slot, not in the title.
Never restate the number in the title; the circle carries it.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Optional body under the step heading: prose, code, or another component.
